title: 28.2 A 189.3dB-FoMs 14.5fJ/Conversion-Step Continuous-Time Noise-Shaping SAR Capacitance-to-Digital Converter
problem: High-resolution capacitance-to-digital converters (CDCs) for IoT environmental monitoring (humidity, pressure) face kT/C and flicker noise limits. ΔΣM-based CDCs offer high resolution via oversampling/noise-shaping but power consumption remains limited by noise floor.
motivation: IoT applications demand power-efficient high-resolution capacitive sensing for environmental monitoring; continuous-time noise-shaping architecture promises superior noise performance at reduced power vs. discrete-time designs.
method: The converter measures capacitance using successive approximation (SAR)—repeatedly comparing the signal to reference values and refining the estimate. It operates continuously instead of waiting for clock pulses, which eliminates timing errors that reduce accuracy. Noise-shaping (mathematically redirecting unwanted electrical noise to high frequencies where it can be filtered) combined with oversampling (taking many measurements) produces a high-resolution digital output.
key_novelty: The core idea is using continuous-time noise-shaping in a successive-approximation (SAR) capacitance-to-digital converter to achieve high resolution while consuming just 14.5 femtojoules per measurement.
contributions: Continuous-time noise-shaping overcoming kT/C and flicker noise limits
Power-efficient CDC for IoT environmental monitoring
primary_theme: continuous-time noise-shaping CDC for IoT sensing
